_comment: Docker seccomp security profile for symfony-agent-mcp (Node.js 20 on Linux x86_64). Uses an allowlist-compatible denylist strategy: defaults to ALLOW and blocks syscalls that are dangerous/unnecessary for an MCP server process. Derived from Docker's default profile with additional MCP-specific restrictions. Apply with: docker run --security-opt seccomp=docker/seccomp.json ...

syscalls.comment: Block process injection. Node.js debugger (--inspect) requires ptrace — do not use that flag in production containers.
Block kernel keyring manipulation — not used by Node.js stdlib.
Block kernel BPF program loading — not needed and is a significant attack surface.
Block hardware performance counters — potential side-channel leak vector.
Block kernel exec — never needed in a container.
Block direct I/O port access — hardware-level privilege escalation vector.
Block system clock modification — container should use host time.
Block system-level operations irrelevant to an MCP server.
Block filesystem manipulation — container filesystem should be immutable.
Block chroot — container already provides filesystem isolation.
Block legacy/admin syscalls not needed by Node.js.
Block user-space page-fault handling — exploitation primitive in several kernel CVEs.
Block NUMA memory policy syscalls — not used by Node.js and occasionally exploitable.
Block x86-specific LDT modification — historical exploitation vector.
Block io_uring — large kernel attack surface; Node.js does not require it for standard I/O.
